races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Grainne A Chroi
runners_data.note: Won last time out and placed on good ground twice in recent history (sim-going: 3/11, 0W2P is misleading given her last-run win at 20f/good); Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a notable asset in a handicap, and sitting prominently just off Birdie Or Bust suits her style perfectly over this trip.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out follows a pulled-up effort, with a win and a second before that, plus proven form over today's distance. Our rating actually nudges her above her official mark, with that pulled-up run the one blot to note.

runners_data.name: Murcia
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 138 and the Mullins-Townend combination carries enormous weight in Irish jumping; won over 16f on good ground last time, now stepping to 2m4½f which is unexplored territory, and that stamina question is the only genuine caveat in what otherwise looks an ideal setup from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: A stretch of moderate finishes was answered with a win last time out, and our rating rates her clear of this field on the back of that improvement. She'll need to confirm the leap after a 47-day break, but the evidence points squarely her way.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Solid form on good ground with a recent win (1/20f/GOO, just 12 days ago) and trainer Elliott in strong recent form (T14: 10/68); a natural prominent racer whose tendency to race close to the pace will be compromised by the crowded front end here — the redistribution to midfield is the key risk to his chance.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out stands out, but a fall and an untidy eighth earlier in the sequence make the overall profile mixed, and our rating leaves her below her official mark. She already holds form over today's distance and is having a quick 12-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners_data.note: Mullins second string at OR 132 ridden by Brian Hayes; his genuine hold-up profile is one of few in this field and he has a course win (1/21f) over similar trip, but his good-going record is poor (0W0P from 2 runs) and 77 days off adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back and already-proven form over today's distance underpin a solid claim, with our rating comfortably clear of the official figure at second of seven. The obvious query is fitness following a lengthy 77-day absence, the one blot on an otherwise strong profile.

runners_data.name: Run For Mahler
runners_data.note: Two wins and five places on good ground (sim-going: 7/8, 2W5P) show strong aptitude for these conditions, and Byrnes has had three winners from 11 runners in the last 14 days; his natural front-running instinct will be blunted by the traffic ahead of him, and his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects the real cost of racing outside his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts show real ability, but her form has since dipped, well beaten in a sixth last time out and a ninth before it, and our rating now sits below her official mark. A 47-day break gives her a chance to bounce back, though that dip is the concern.

runners_data.name: Birdie Or Bust
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter and the race-shaper here; De Bromhead and Cobden represent a strong team and his two wins have come over 18f on soft, so both the step up to 2m4½f and the good ground are being asked of him simultaneously — the STYLE_FIT flag suggests his chance as a winner is discounted even as he controls the race.
runners_data.comment: A workmanlike third last time out follows a mixed spell including a pulled-up run and a well-beaten ninth, but there's a win in the book and she already holds form over today's distance. Our rating does leave her a touch below her official mark, the one query against an otherwise solid claim.

runners_data.name: Taketwotoone
runners_data.note: A 189-day absence, an OR of just 88, and a form string of 8/008- on heavy ground with a clear tendency to fade in the finish make him a very difficult proposition in any scenario; amateur rider Mr T O'Connor adds further risk in a hurdle over this distance against seasoned rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with well-beaten eighths either side of two unplaced efforts in between, and a 189-day absence adds to the concerns. She does hold form over today's distance, and our rating sits well above her official mark, but there's little to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Birdie Or Bust is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only seven runners over 2m4½f, should be able to dictate an honest but manageable gallop without being pressured into suicidal fractions — creating conditions where the leader can be tracked cleanly and stamina becomes the deciding factor rather than explosive finishing speed. Grainne A Chroi and Murcia will look to press or sit prominently just off the pace, meaning the race is likely to have a compact, organised shape through the middle stages with little chaos or pace collapse. This field actually contains more genuine prominent-runners than the race can accommodate in that position: Run For Mahler and Ardeen Joy are natural front-to-prominent types who will be forced to sit in a midfield role they do not usually occupy, compromising their ability to control their own race. The resulting shape — a single front-runner setting a sustainable pace with several prominent types tracking — strongly favours a horse who can sit second or third, travel comfortably throughout, and prove their stamina over the trip when the race quickens off the final bend; Murcia and Grainne A Chroi are best placed to exploit that platform.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Birdie Or Bust Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Birdie Or Bust sets a measured, unchallenged pace and the prominent trackers are unable to sustain a winning challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Birdie Or Bust dictates from the front at a gallop that suits his jumping rhythm, and the race effectively becomes a test of who has trained sharpest and who can match his stamina at the distance; horses sitting second and third travelling well throughout have the ideal platform to pounce, making this a scenario for the prominent trackers rather than the leader himself given his STYLE_FIT discount.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Murcia and Grainne A Chroi track Birdie Or Bust fluently and the front-runner weakens approaching the final flight, leaving those two to fight out the finish.
scenarios.body: Murcia, trained by Mullins and ridden by Townend, has the class advantage at OR 138 and is proven on good ground, making him the most dangerous beneficiary of this shape; Grainne A Chroi's recent form (win last time, placed on similar going) makes her a credible second string if Murcia finds the trip beyond him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and Diamond Du Berlais, a genuine hold-up type, is delivered with a single sweeping run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Diamond Du Berlais has won over this sort of trip (1/21f/SOF) and has the freshness of 77 days off, but his record on good ground specifically is thin with no wins or places from two runs, which limits confidence in this scenario; Brian Hayes would need the race to be truly run to suit for him to bridge the gap from the back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types push forward and create an overly strong early pace that collapses the field, allowing a fresher or better-stamina horse to emerge late.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Birdie Or Bust's uncontested lead role, but if Run For Mahler or Ardeen Joy do fight for position and accelerate the early fractions, attrition through the final mile could produce a surprising result; Taketwotoone's poor recent form and lengthy absence (189 days) make him a very unlikely beneficiary even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Murcia's stamina for 2m4½f is unproven — watch how he travels into the home turn; if he shortens stride before the last two flights the trip has found him out and Grainne A Chroi inherits the race.

Run For Mahler and Ardeen Joy may both look to push forward at the start, potentially creating a brief but sharp early injection of pace that pressures Birdie Or Bust before the halfway point — watch the early fractions.

Birdie Or Bust has won on soft (twice) but has a thin record on good ground (sim-going 11/15, though 2W4P); if the pace drains him before the straight, the entire race shape collapses and Diamond Du Berlais becomes live.

Taketwotoone has been off 189 days and shown a consistent pattern of fading finishes — if he is still travelling at the second-last, it would represent a significant deviation from his profile and would merit attention as a market clue about something unseen in the data.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Swelltime
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer at age 10 with a winning run on good going 14 days ago, though the fade-in-finish flag is a notable concern; will need things to go wrong for others in the straight to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Swelltime won one of his last five starts and returns quickly on a 14-day turnaround, with today's distance already under his belt; our rating nudges him a shade above his official mark, though he'll need to bounce back from a couple of below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: 200 days off the track is a major flag for a six-year-old; showed a placed effort on good ground historically but the long layoff undermines confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Luck Between Us is winless in his last five starts, though a third-placed effort in that spell shows he stays competitive, and today's trip is proven ground for him; a 200-day absence since his last run is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Malikanna
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter who will likely go forward unchallenged, though the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 suggests this isn't its most natural role; its control of the race shapes outcomes more than its own winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Malikanna is winless in her last five starts but a runner-up effort in that sequence hints at real ability, and she already goes well over today's trip; her profile is mixed, though, with a fall among her recent starts leaving durability a slight question.

runners_data.name: King Ferdinand
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old prominent racer with strong good-ground credentials (12/15 sim-going) and multiple wins on this type of surface; the experience and tactical position racing just off Malikanna makes him a key player in Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: King Ferdinand's finishing efforts have been workmanlike at best, with a pulled-up and an unseated among his last five outings, yet our rating puts him well above his official mark, and today's distance is already within his range — such indifferent form leaves obvious questions.

runners_data.name: Papagei
runners_data.note: Only four days since last run is an eyecatcher, whether positive (fit) or negative (quick turnaround); hold-up style on good ground but no wins yet in 15 similar-going runs.
runners_data.comment: Papagei is out again quickly, just four days after his latest run, and already holds today's trip within his compass, but his form has been modest throughout, with nothing better than a 4th in his last five starts and a fall among them.

runners_data.name: Gaoithe Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has never placed on good ground specifically, going 0W0P in seven relevant runs; headgear noted but the form figures don't inspire confidence in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Gaoithe Glory has been no better than 4th in his last five starts, with two 9th-placed efforts mixed in, but he already holds today's trip and returns from a workable 49-day break; the form reads moderate rather than smart, leaving him plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Excellent record on good ground (13/15 runs, four wins, seven places), acts over this sort of trip, headgear noted, prominent racer well-suited to tracking a single front-runner — one of the standout beneficiaries of this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Inchidaly Copper won one of his last five starts and has been competitive throughout, with two 3rd-placed efforts in that sequence; he steps back out on a quick 14-day turnaround with today's trip already proven, though his latest effort was a below-par 8th.

runners_data.name: Koeur A Prendre
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose best run (second last time) came on good ground, but the redistribution into midfield means it cannot produce its natural game; discounted in most scenarios accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Koeur A Prendre is winless in his last four starts but signed off with a promising 2nd last time out, and he already holds today's trip within his range; a 63-day gap since that effort is the main concern before he can back it up.

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: A young four-year-old with an alarming recent form string of P-P and a thin record on comparable going (3/15); distance and form both raise serious doubts.
runners_data.comment: Ray Gun has managed nothing better than 8th in his last five starts, a sequence blighted by two pulled-up efforts, and his latest run 50 days ago was another below-par display; the profile offers little encouragement without a return to form.

runners_data.name: Brianna Lily
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who naturally wants to come from off the pace but will be squeezed into midfield with numerous rivals; the style compromise and modest form figures make this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Brianna Lily is winless in her last five starts, though a 3rd-placed effort three runs back shows she has ability, and today's trip suits; our rating sits well above her official mark, but her last two efforts have been modest, capped by an 8th.

runners_data.name: Boston Queen
runners_data.note: Trained by Gordon Elliott (strong 14-day strike rate of 10/68) which is worth noting, but the fade-in-finish flag and a blank recent record (0W0P on good) make it hard to construct a winning scenario; its true hold-up style is further hampered by being mapped forward.
runners_data.comment: Boston Queen's recent form is hard to recommend, with two 9th-placed finishes and a brought-down among her last five starts; our rating leaves her firmly at the bottom of this field, with little in the facts to suggest a turnaround.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Consistent midfield to hold-up performer on good ground (14/15 runs) but zero wins in those appearances; the headgear suggests connections are searching, and the style compromise adds another layer of difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Mother Ship is winless in her last five starts, though a runner-up effort in that sequence shows some scope, and today's trip already suits; the yard is out of form, though, having gone winless with its last 30 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Tedworth
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 20f and has run on this surface type 15 times — experience is real; naturally wants to come from behind but among the redistributed horses has the most credible finishing form to capitalise if gaps materialise.
runners_data.comment: Tedworth won once in his last five starts, sandwiched among finishes of 4th, unplaced and 4th again, and was unseated last time out; today's trip is proven, but the overall profile reads workmanlike rather than progressive.

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Non-runner status makes this entry void for betting purposes; noted only for completeness — the fade-in-finish flag and blank good-ground record (0W0P) were already against it.
runners_data.comment: Beacon Bypass's recent form offers little to shout about, with unplaced efforts twice and a 9th among his last five starts, and our rating actually rates him below his official mark; there's little in the facts to make a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Pleasureofpressure
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose trainer has a 2/21 14-day strike rate — modest but active; consistent placed efforts on good ground (0W1P but multiple fourths) suggest it runs its race every time without quite winning.
runners_data.comment: Pleasureofpressure is winless in his last five starts but has been a model of consistency, never finishing worse than 4th, including a 2nd four runs back; today's trip is already proven, though he still needs to prove he can go one better.

runners_data.name: Miss Donna
runners_data.note: A five-year-old prominent racer with placed form on good ground; 41 days fresh is fine, headgear noted, and 2m4½f is further than her recent runs — the extra distance is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Miss Donna is winless in her last five starts, though she signed off with a promising 3rd last time out, and today's trip already suits; our rating sits above her official mark, but two 8th-placed efforts earlier in that sequence temper the picture.

races.paceDynamic: Malikanna is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and is likely to dictate at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front, with King Ferdinand and Inchidaly Copper tracking closely in the prominent positions. Pleasureofpressure and Miss Donna will also push forward, meaning the early sections will be organised rather than frantic, creating a true-run but not pressured pace over 2m4½f on good ground. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Koeur A Prendre, Brianna Lily, Boston Queen, Mother Ship, Tedworth, and Beacon Bypass are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will be forced to race in midfield against their natural instincts, meaning their finishing kicks may be compromised. The sustainable pace set by Malikanna, combined with several closers crowded into midfield, strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel well into the straight — front-runners and prominent-racers who conserve energy early before asserting from the second-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malikanna Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Malikanna sets a sustainable gallop and the prominent trackers King Ferdinand and Inchidaly Copper travel smoothly into contention from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Malikanna's uncontested lead creates a false-economy scenario where those racing just behind in positions two to four enjoy the optimum race — saved early, close enough to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find A Lane
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to soften the front-runners and a handful of the overcrowded midfield horses manage to find clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: Despite the redistribution crowding, a true galloper like Koeur A Prendre or Tedworth — who has proven form on good ground — could benefit if the field spreads wide and gaps appear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Malikanna settles exceptionally well in front and is never seriously challenged, effectively converting the race into a test of relentless, controlled attrition.
scenarios.body: At 2m4½f on good ground, a front-runner who has its own way can simply never come off the bridle and pick up from the final hurdle; Pleasureofpressure, racing prominently, could also benefit from this shape by staying on doggedly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overrun Tiring Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight as the front-runners tire and the overcrowded midfield horses collectively swarm over them in the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the sustainable pace projection and the number of hold-up horses compromised by their unnatural midfield positions, but Swelltime — a genuine hold-up type with good going form — could capitalise on a chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Inchidaly Copper's prominent racing style and exceptional good-ground record (13/15, four wins) make it the clearest tactical beneficiary of Malikanna's uncontested lead — watch for it to travel ominously into the straight.

Malikanna's behaviour in front is the race's fulcrum — if it is swamped early by King Ferdinand or Pleasureofpressure pushing forward, the pace dynamic could change sharply and compress the race shape.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Koeur A Prendre, Tedworth, Brianna Lily, Mother Ship, Boston Queen — will create significant midfield congestion; watch for traffic trouble approaching the final three hurdles that could affect any of them.

Tedworth, despite being redistributed into midfield against its natural style, has the most convincing winning form on good ground among the hold-up brigade — it could still find a run if the field fans wide on the turn in.
Papagei's four-day turnaround is worth monitoring in the parade ring; if the horse looks sharp and well, the quick return could signal connections have spotted an opportunity in this division.

races.name: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tuche De Houelle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old whose running style is uncertain; has handled good ground and showed ability at Killarney (4th, 16f, good), but the unknown role and sparse career profile make it difficult to place confidence in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in the last four starts, including one just two runs back, mark this out as the form horse in the race, backed up by our rating topping the entire field. A below-par fourth last time out, after a rapid 14-day turnaround, is the one blot to note.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner, set to dictate for Gavin Cromwell; strong record in similar going (13/15 sim-going qualifies) but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.92 signals this prominent role on a tight map, and at 10 years old stamina in the final climb needs monitoring.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency with three frame finishes from the last five starts, including a win three runs back, and he already holds form over today's distance. The yard's poor recent strike rate is a mild concern, but his own solid recent form makes the stronger case here.

runners_data.name: Global Skies
runners_data.note: In-form five-year-old who won last two starts over this trip on good ground at this course — the course and distance form is a major positive; Ross O'Sullivan's stable is firing (3/20 in 14 days) and Danny Gilligan takes the ride on a horse ideally suited to tracking the pace.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins in the last two starts mark a big turnaround from a mixed run of results before that, and he already holds form over today's distance with barely a fortnight since his latest success. Our rating is still a touch below his official mark, so there's a question over whether the improvement fully sticks.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: 133 days off the track, unknown going preference, and an uncertain running style — too many question marks to project with confidence; the lightly raced profile and amateur jockey (Michael Kenneally, 5lb claim) add to the risk.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and still winless, with finishes of sixth, fourth, unplaced and third across four starts, there's more promise in that profile than the bare results suggest. A lengthy 133-day absence raises the obvious fitness question, but the placed efforts hint at more to come once he gets going again.

runners_data.name: Kazakh d'Arthel
runners_data.note: Has winning form on good ground over similar trips for Gavin Cromwell; Keith Donoghue is an experienced partner but the recent form string (414F-0) and pulled-up run raise fitness and jumping questions that temper enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: A win in the book and a rating above his official mark suggest more ability than the bare figures show. But the recent script is concerning — an unplaced effort last time out followed a fall the run before — with the yard's poor recent strike rate adding to the worry.

runners_data.name: Only For Our Man
runners_data.note: Consistent horse who has placed in all four qualifying starts on good ground, winning once over 22f; held up in blinkers which suit a prominent-to-pressing style, and the 47-day break for Paul Nolan's yard is not a concern given the record.
runners_data.comment: The model of consistency, with four frame finishes from the last five starts including a win three runs back, but he has been runner-up in each of his last two starts since, suggesting he lacks that final change of gear. Our rating sits just a shade below his official mark, in keeping with a solid but unspectacular profile.

runners_data.name: Market Ready
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent type whose jumping and form are tuned to racing handy, but the redistribution to hold-up on the pace map means it will likely be held further back than ideal — that positional compromise will make it harder to land a blow from an unfamiliar rear position.
runners_data.comment: Rock-solid for consistency with a top-four finish in each of his last five starts, and our rating rates him well clear of his official mark, third of ten in this field. The query is that he remains yet to win, so the finishing effort to get his head in front is unproven.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Won twice off a prominent berth and is a natural front-rank racer; pushed into midfield here purely because the field is stacked with prominent types — racing against its instincts at a 4-day turnaround for John Patrick Ryan, who is in form (3/17 in 14 days), adds layers of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in these last five, and a below-par effort last time out follows a promising second before that, for a patchy overall picture. He's fresh on just four days' rest, already holds form over today's distance, and our rating actually places him above his official mark — some encouragement amid the inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Won last time out (19f, good) and boasts solid sim-going form (7/15); another natural front-runner squeezed off its preferred pitch by the congested prominent ranks — the positional disadvantage blunts what is otherwise an in-form profile on the right surface.
runners_data.comment: A solid second last time out, following a win two starts back, marks his best recent form; our rating nudges him above his official mark and he has proven form over today's distance. The form earlier in the sequence was modest, leaving him towards the rear on these figures.

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish; returned a placed effort last time (2nd, 20f, good) but has a poor record in similar going overall (6/10 with no wins) and the fade tag makes it difficult to see this horse reversing that pattern at the business end.
runners_data.comment: A promising second last time out is the shining light in an otherwise substandard sequence that includes a spell pulled up and finishes well down the field, and he remains winless in this form. Our rating does edge him a shade above his official mark, but ranked ninth of ten there's little more to recommend him.

races.paceDynamic: Arcland is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press them from the outset, Eoghan Finegan can dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m4½f trip on good ground. Global Skies and Kazakh d'Arthel are the most likely to sit prominently just off the pace, with Only For Our Man also capable of tracking the leader, meaning the front half of the field will be well populated. The field is overloaded with prominent-running types — Smallcraftwarning and Blue Reed are both natural front-rank horses who cannot all claim their preferred berth and will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, diminishing their effectiveness. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel sweetly just off the pace and produce a clean turn of foot in the straight, rather than genuine hold-up horses or those forced wide of their comfort zone.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arcland Dictates, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Arcland bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest enough to soften the field without being a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Arcland sets a measured gallop and those tracking just behind — Global Skies and Only For Our Man — travel within themselves before producing their challenge from the second-last; the even tempo suits horses with a genuine turn of foot rather than out-and-out stayers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Arcland goes too slow and the race turns into a sprint finish from two out.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian gallop compresses the field and removes Arcland's stamina edge, turning the contest into a flat-out dash for home; horses with a sharp finishing kick and enough tactical speed to be close enough late benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Arcland Capitulates, Chaser Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Arcland's age (10) tells in the closing stages and a pressing rival moves through to collar them.
scenarios.body: A prominent stalker takes over approaching the final hurdle as Arcland's effort flattens out; this scenario rewards a horse like Only For Our Man or Global Skies who has the cruising speed to hold position and the finishing reserves to see it out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Open Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field fractures early with multiple horses scrapping for the front and the pace becomes ragged.
scenarios.body: Disruption at the head of affairs causes trouble in running and opens the race to a horse delivered from off the pace; Speakasyoufind or a hold-up type finding a clear run late could grab a piece of the prize, though this shape depends on horses racing against type.

watchPoints.text: Arcland's jumping — if they make a significant error early, the entire pace plan unravels and the race shape collapses before it forms; monitor hurdle one and two closely.

Blue Reed and Smallcraftwarning are both natural front-runners who will be pushing for position early despite being mapped to midfield — any scrimmaging or crowding in the first half-mile could cause interference for those tracking the pace.

Global Skies has won twice at this course and trip on good ground; if Danny Gilligan secures an uninterrupted run just off Arcland's shoulder, the course and distance form marks this horse as the most obvious danger to the leader.

Jupiter Du Gite is 133 days off the track with a completely unknown going profile — watch for any unexpected move in the market pre-race as that would be the principal signal of confidence from connections.

Speakasyoufind's hold-up role and fade tendency means Simon Torrens will need a trouble-free passage and a strong pace to set up a finish — if the tempo is too slow, this horse's chance effectively disappears before the last.

races.name: Kerry Drains Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gavin Cromwell with a win over 18f on good ground in recent form (1-form string) — 3 from 6 on similar going is solid, and Eoghan Finegan (5) claiming weight is a bonus; 32 days fresh and dropped back slightly in field quality at OR 113.
runners_data.comment: Kamino Bello is our second-rated on 115, with today's trip already proven and a workable 32-day break since his last run. He won five starts back but the yard is ice cold (1/45, 2% last 14 days) and finishes have been modest since.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Consistent on good ground with 8 from 8 similar-going runs placing in the frame, but no wins in that recent sequence and a 67-day break for a trainer with no runners in the last 14 days raises freshness doubts; tongue-tie fitted, hold-up style suits a genuine pace but this record trends to minor honours.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and pulled up two back, Claude nonetheless holds claims on our figures — 119 here compares with an official mark of just 107. Today's trip is already proven, though a 67-day absence adds a slight question mark.

runners_data.name: Kabylia
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form and good ground figures (9 from 11 on similar), wearing a hood and tongue-tie combination; the Cromwell yard has a runner in form (1/45 T14) and Keith Donoghue takes over in the saddle — finished 2nd twice at 17f on good, this trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Kabylia shaped well with a 3rd and a 2nd four and five starts back over today's trip, but has since faded to 6th and 9th. Our figures still rate her 8 lb clear of her official mark, though a 51-day gap and a cold yard (1/45, 2%) add concern.

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who makes the pace here by default, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a genuine caution — recent form shows a win at 16f on good but the record at this sort of trip and this type of field is mixed; Cian Collins has had only 6 runners in 14 days with no winners, and Secret Rock's ability to sustain a quality gallop over 2m1f is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Secret Rock won last time out and again four starts back, sandwiching two 5th-placed efforts, and he's proven over today's trip. Our rating of 109 nudges his official mark of 105, though a 46-day absence is the one query.

runners_data.name: Lips Freedom
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a stamina win on soft over 18f but the "fades in finish" flag is damaging here — three of last five runs show double-figure finishes on good ground, and 109 days off the track after a win on soft could mean the good surface blunts the effort late.
runners_data.comment: Lips Freedom returns off a 109-day break having won on his latest start, though a string of unplaced efforts beforehand and our figures 6 lb below his official mark temper the enthusiasm. He does have today's trip in his locker.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two wins on good ground and a second last time on soft at 16f — 16 days since last run keeps him fresh, and Dylan O'Connor (7) claims weight for a handler with limited recent runners; the 19f run (9th) is a mild concern over this 2m1f trip but form trajectory is positive.
runners_data.comment: Party President was a clear second two starts back and is fresh into this race just 16 days after his latest run, with today's trip already safely negotiated. He's yet to win in his last five starts and pulled up three back, but our figures have him well clear of his official mark.

runners_data.name: Katakana
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last win came on good ground over 16f — 244 days off the track is a significant flag, Henry De Bromhead's yard has been active (5/35 T14) but this is a big absence to overcome; sitting further forward than ideal due to redistribution, the STYLE_FIT score tempers expectations even on a return to good ground.
runners_data.comment: Katakana won two starts back over today's trip but was well beaten either side of that success, and finished unplaced last time out. A 244-day absence is a major concern, though our figures still nudge her 3 lb clear of her official mark.

runners_data.name: Mc Swagger
runners_data.note: Unraced-code flagged with a "fades in finish" warning, finishing outside the first three in all recent starts on good ground; the 37-day break and OR 102 put this in a tough spot, and a pull-up in the form string adds a welfare/fitness question mark.
runners_data.comment: Mc Swagger has found little in a mixed run that includes an unseated-rider effort and finished unplaced last time out, without a win in his last five starts. Today's trip is proven and he arrives fit enough from a 37-day gap, with our figures sitting him only a shade above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Returned just 10 days ago (4th at 16f good) so fitness is clear, but this true hold-up horse is pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of closers in this race — the STYLE_FIT (0.90) is the lowest in the field, and two of four runs on good have produced minor placings at best over shorter trips than today.
runners_data.comment: Home By The Sea has shown modest form, two unplaced efforts sandwiched between an early 5th and a 4th last time out, and remains without a win in his last four starts. He is fresh into this race just 10 days after his latest run and has today's trip proven, but our figures leave him 5 lb below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Regards To Rose
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good and placed twice at OR 100 — a hold-up performer who is funnelled into midfield on this map but whose natural operating position is further back than the map suggests; lightly raced at 7f+ trips with a tongue-tie, and 14 days between runs is fine, but the redistribution genuinely compromises the chance in a race with few true pace-makers.
runners_data.comment: Regards To Rose won three starts back over today's trip but has since faded to 8th and 9th, her last two efforts. A quick 14-day turnaround keeps her ticking over, and our figures still have her 4 lb clear of her official mark.

runners_data.name: Rattledelatch
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has never placed in four runs on good ground, with the best finish a 6th — headgear flag (hood) and the redistribution note both apply, as this horse is naturally a deeper hold-up type squeezed into midfield; OR 99 and limited form on good makes this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Rattledelatch is unexposed on these figures and remains without a win in his last four starts, though his 6th last time out was the best of the four. A 40-day gap adds a slight question mark.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Two wins in the form string over 17f on good ground and active in the last fortnight — Shane O'Callaghan (3) claims and P J Rothwell's yard has had two winners in 14 days (2/21), making the trainer angle live; this horse is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is further back than shown, but the recent form (4th, 1st) and going affinity are hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Kilt won two starts back and followed up with a fair 4th last time out, having been unplaced and 7th in the two runs before that success. A brisk 13-day turnaround keeps him fresh, and our figures have him 3 lb clear of his official mark, though he faces a stiff task in this field.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has been outside the first three in all five recent runs, with one third over 20f on good being the career best; the redistribution to midfield is doubly awkward for a horse who needs a strong pace to close into — OR 92 and this pattern makes it hard to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Eagle has managed only a 3rd among a string of unplaced efforts, including last time out, and remains winless in her last five starts. Our figures nonetheless have her fully 11 lb clear of her official mark, with a fair 32-day gap since her latest run.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: Three runs for Eoin McCarthy's yard in the last month with a 6th last time — the "fades in finish" flag and tongue-tie are both negatives, and the redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up position compounds the problem; OR 87 is the softest rating in the field and this horse has not won on good ground.
runners_data.comment: Kingdom Calling remains without a win in his last five starts, undone by a pulled-up effort and finishing unplaced twice including last time out. Our figures rate him a striking 19 lb above his official mark, though, and a snug 16-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent runner with two seconds in the form string over longer trips (20-24f) on good ground — 277 days off the track is a serious concern for the first run back, but the tongue-tie is retained and David Harry Kelly's horse has been placed at this sort of trip before; the prominent style suits this race shape, but the absence length at age nine is the obvious risk.
runners_data.comment: Corkbeg was runner-up twice with a third mixed in earlier in his recent form, but that promise has faded, and he was down the field when ninth on his latest start. A 277-day absence is a serious concern, and our figures leave him only a shade above his official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Rock is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Kabylia and Corkbeg as the only other genuinely prominent types, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching across 2m1f on good ground at Killarney — Secret Rock can bowl along at a comfortable gallop and control tempo without being seriously challenged for the lead. The field is saturated with hold-up horses: Katakana, Regards To Rose, Home By The Sea, Kilt, Rattledelatch, Midnight Eagle and Kingdom Calling are all genuine closers who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them all to operate from their natural position at the rear, meaning those redistribution tags carry real weight when assessing race shape. With a lone, unfettered pace-setter setting a moderate to sustainable tempo, the race is likely to develop as a cavalry charge from mid-race, with ground to make up in the straight — this shape favours runners who can travel prominently or close through the field with purpose rather than pure hold-up reliance. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers and horses with a high cruising speed that can sit just off the leader will be best placed, while genuine deep closers face a significant disadvantage if the pace proves insufficient to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Secret Rock Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Rock bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but unfrenetic pace that rewards those travelling prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Secret Rock dictates from the front without pressure, keeping the gallop honest enough to expose hold-up horses who can't quicken from too far back; Kabylia and Corkbeg, travelling just off the leader, are best positioned to pounce turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Rock sets a genuinely slow tempo that turns the race into a sprint finish, allowing the better-rated closers to close the gap rapidly.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race opens the door for the hold-up horses who can produce a strong late burst, though many of the redistributed closers are operating out of their ideal position in this field; the better-quality hold-up runners with strong finishing form get the clearest run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Rises, Stamina Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Kabylia or another prominent type pushes Secret Rock into a genuine gallop early, raising the tempo and turning it into a thorough stamina test.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace stretches the field and grinds down those with any doubt over the 2m1f trip on good ground; the more experienced, thorough stayers who handle a good surface come into their own late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Big Field Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the 15-runner field generates interference, fallers or significant traffic problems that disrupt the pace picture entirely.
scenarios.body: Crowded jumps races at Killarney over 2m1f can produce scrimmaging at early hurdles, leaving horses out of position and nullifying tactical plans; the most adaptable and robust traveller with a clear passage benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Secret Rock sets the pace alone — if Kabylia or Corkbeg push up to press from the early stages, the tempo could rise sharply and fundamentally alter which scenario unfolds.

The field of 15 over hurdles at Killarney creates a genuine crowding risk at the early flights — any horse carrying a redistribution tag and sitting in an unnatural position (Katakana, Home By The Sea, Kilt) is vulnerable to being hampered or checked.
Corkbeg's 277-day absence is the longest in the field — if the horse returns rusty or short of peak fitness, the prominent style that suits this race shape will not be fully exploited.

Kamino Bello and Party President are the two hold-up horses with the cleanest recent form and going credentials — watch how much daylight they have approaching the final flight, as a clear run from there is likely decisive for either.

Katakana's 244-day layoff combined with the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) means Darragh O'Keeffe may need to push forward earlier than ideal to be competitive — if he does, the pace dynamic tightens and Scenario C becomes more plausible.
